rounds.text: Ravita Engineering Services Ltd trades at a modest P/E of 16x [E1] while delivering extraordinary fundamental performance, including an ROE of 48.9% [E8] and an ROCE of 48.17% [E9], both vastly outperforming sector benchmarks of 10.51% and 12.53% respectively. Growth metrics are equally compelling, featuring a 3-year compounded sales growth of 146% [E13] and an astonishing 3-year compounded profit growth of 534% [E15]. Furthermore, the operating margin has expanded by 9 percentage points to reach 14% by March 2026 [E19]. The balance sheet remains conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.19x, alongside borrowings that decreased to Rs 19 Cr [E25, E26]. Valuation models indicate significant mispricing, as a discounted cash flow analysis sets intrinsic value at Rs 302 against a current market price of Rs 119 [E29], providing a substantial margin of safety of 60.6% [E30]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative at Rs -47 Cr for March 2026, leading to a weak cash conversion of -1.68x [E22, E23].

Despite headline profitability metrics, Ravita Engineering Services Ltd suffers from a severe fundamental disconnect between reported earnings and actual cash generation [E22]. Operating cash flow and free cash flow for March 2026 both collapsed to negative Rs 47 Cr, resulting in an alarming cash conversion ratio of -1.68x against reported profit [E22, E23, E24]. This cash drain is directly compounded by a structural deterioration in liquidity, evidenced by working capital days surging significantly from 65.4 days to 112 days [E36]. Furthermore, the company carries a flagged accounting risk that it might be capitalizing interest costs, casting doubt on the true quality of its financial statements [E35]. Adding to investor caution, the stock offers a dividend yield of 0.00%, returning nothing to shareholders while cash burns [E3]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong historical return metrics such as an ROE of 48.9% and a 3-year compounded profit growth of 534% [E12, E15].

Conceded: operating cash flow and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs 47 Cr in March 2026, and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E3, E23, E24]. However, this cash crunch occurs against a backdrop of exceptional fundamental growth, including a 3-year compounded profit growth of 534% and a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 137% [E15, E16]. The bear highlights rising working capital days to 112 days, but this must be contextualized against explosive top-line acceleration, with 3-year sales growth at 146% and TTM sales growth at 156% [E13, E14, E36]. Regarding the flagged interest capitalization risk [E35], the company's underlying operating profitability remains elite, boasting an ROCE of 48.17% and an ROE of 48.9%, both vastly outperforming sector benchmarks of 12.53% and 10.51% [E8, E9]. Furthermore, despite these cash flow headwinds, borrowings were actively reduced from Rs 23 Cr to Rs 19 Cr, leaving the business conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.19x [E25, E26].

Conceded: 3-year compounded profit growth reached 534% and trailing twelve-month profit growth hit 137% [E15, E16]. Conceded: 3-year sales growth is 146% and TTM sales growth is 156% [E13, E14]. Conceded: ROE stands at 48.9% and ROCE at 48.17% [E8, E9]. Conceded: borrowings decreased from Rs 23 Cr to Rs 19 Cr with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.19x [E25, E26]. However, dismissing the cash crunch and the spike in working capital days to 112 days ignores the reality that operating cash flow and free cash flow both collapsed to negative Rs 47 Cr in March 2026, delivering a devastating cash conversion of -1.68x [E22, E23, E24, E36]. Furthermore, the bull fails to defend against the explicit warning flag that the company might be capitalizing its interest cost, which severely undermines the credibility of those headline profit figures [E35].
